hardware_summary: On-site captive gas turbine generator (GTG) plant, 13 MW, supplying part of the terminal's power alongside grid import; separate 1.6 MVA diesel emergency DG set for backup (non-gas, informational only).
fuel_basis: MoEFCC/environmentclearance.nic.in Form A filing lists 'GTG' (gas turbine generator) as a distinct equipment item alongside 'EDG' (emergency diesel generator) in the same noise-source inventory, and separately states the 13 MW captive plant is '(GTGs)' - i.e. gas turbine generators, distinguished from the diesel EDG.
captive_summary: Kochi LNG Terminal (Petronet) is partially self-powered: a 13 MW on-site captive gas turbine generator (GTG) plant supplies part of the terminal's electricity, topped up by Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) grid power. A separate 1.6 MVA diesel emergency DG set exists purely for backup (diesel, not gas, so not itself a captive-gas finding but confirms the GTGs are the gas-fired plant).
confirmed_how: Primary/regulatory source: MoEFCC environmental clearance 'Report Part 1' (Form A) for Kochi LNG Terminal, hosted at environmentclearance.nic.in (proposal IA/KL/IND2/229000/2021), states verbatim: 'The source of power for the existing LNG terminal is from captive power Plant of capacity 13 MW (GTGs) and KSEB (Kerala State Electricity Board). Also, one Emergency DG set of capacity 1.6 MVA is installed for emergency power backup.' The same document's noise-inventory table separately lists 'GTG' alongside 'EDG', 'BOG Compressors, Pumps, vaporizers... SCV' confirming GTG and EDG are distinct plant items (gas turbine vs diesel generator). Corroborated by Petronet LNG's own procurement/NIT document (petronetlng.in), which lists a 'Captive gas power plant' among the Kochi terminal's utility infrastructure.

verification_log.note: MoEFCC Form A / Report Part 1 for Kochi LNG Terminal; all three tokens found verbatim.
Petronet LNG's own NIT/tender document listing terminal utilities.

gogpt_prior_assessment: gogpt_prior was 'no' - no GOGPT plant was pre-matched to this terminal for review. The 13 MW captive GTG plant found here does not appear to have an existing GOGPT record under Kochi/Puthuvypeen search terms based on this research pass.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Genuine, sourced, gas-fired generating plant (GTGs) with a citable nameplate (13 MW) from a primary regulatory filing - meets the ADD bar at any size.
notes: Partially-captive site: GTGs + KSEB grid, both feeding the terminal (captive counts per SOP even when partial). Diesel EDG (1.6 MVA) is backup-only and non-gas, so it does not itself qualify, but its explicit listing alongside GTG in the source is what nails the fuel distinction.

captive_summary: Mundra LNG Terminal (GSPC LNG Ltd / Adani, commissioned Jan 2020, 5 MMTPA within Mundra SEZ) has no publicly documented statement of its own power supply arrangement - neither a captive gas-fired generation plant nor a grid-connection statement was found in any searchable source.
confirmed_how: Extensive search across multiple engines (Bing web + RSS, Brave, DuckDuckGo html/lite, Google, Ecosia, Mojeek, Marginalia) and direct document pulls found: (1) the terminal's own project pages (Petronet/GSPC/Adani, offshore-technology.com, Wood Mackenzie) describe capacity/ownership/commissioning but never the power-supply arrangement; (2) environmentclearance.nic.in filings found under 'Mundra LNG' search terms belong to co-located but DIFFERENT projects - the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery 'Arab Mix Crude Oil Pipeline' EC filing (cat_id IA/GJ/IND2/137870/2020, itself stating a 5 MW grid-sourced load for an unrelated crude pipeline) and the Mundra-Anjar natural-gas send-out pipeline transfer letters (GSPC LNG Ltd to Gujarat State Petronet Ltd) - none of which describe the LNG terminal's own utility power. No EC/EIA document specific to the LNG terminal's own power source (as found for Kochi) could be located. This is a genuine public-record gap, not a documented negative.
gogpt_prior_assessment: gogpt_prior 'no' - no GOGPT plant assigned; not applicable, insufficient finding.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Power-supply arrangement genuinely undisclosed; cannot rule a captive plant in or out, so a possible cogeneration/captive plant cannot be assessed for a GOGPT nameplate at this time.
status_or_other_findings: Direction-test note (not a captive finding): press coverage indicates Mundra LNG Terminal supplies regasified gas via the Mundra-Anjar pipeline to downstream customers including a ~700 MW gas-fired power plant (reported as GSPC's Pipavav facility) - this is the OUTPUT direction (terminal feeds an external power plant), the opposite of captive power, and is a PowerPlantsSupplied-type relationship for a different batch, not evidence of this terminal's own power source.
notes: Grid-access prior would suggest NO (modern, 2020-commissioned, grid-rich Mundra SEZ industrial site with heavy GETCO/PGVCL transmission infrastructure nearby) but no documented statement was found either way, so the verdict is INSUFFICIENT rather than NO per the brief's rule that absence of evidence is not a documented negative.
